flashcard_questions.q: Which FBI director built a vast surveillance network to root out communists?
What did the initials HUAC stand for?
What name was given to the ten writers and directors who refused to answer HUAC's questions?
How many people were blacklisted by the Hollywood studios?
Which comedian left America for Switzerland rather than face investigation?
Which 1953 play by Arthur Miller was an allegory for McCarthyism?
Which State Department official did Whittaker Chambers accuse of spying for the USSR?
What crime was Alger Hiss convicted of in January 1950?
On what date were the Rosenbergs executed?
On what date did McCarthy first claim to have a list of communists in the State Department?
How many communists did McCarthy claim were working in the State Department?
Which executive order set up the Federal Employee Loyalty Program in 1947?
How many government workers were checked for disloyalty between 1947 and 1953?
Which lawyer asked McCarthy, 'Have you no sense of decency, sir, at long last?'
How did the Senate vote in December 1954 on censuring McCarthy?

notes: 15 cards: 6 person to significance, 4 statistic, 3 event to date, 2 term or act to name. Dropped the First Amendment card and the Army-McCarthy viewing figure to stay inside 15; the civil-liberties section is evaluation rather than card material.
